KZN NEXT LEVEL LANDGRAB

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Next Level Landgrabs in KZN – where mansions have illegally been built on government land by wealthy landgrabbers – we ask what the Msunduzi Municipality is doing to curb this alarming trend.

Unique Selling Point:
SHOCK VALUE - the audacity of the people that have built mansions with fountains and pools on stolen land.
WHY DO IT? Undercover, a confront and a municipality trying to make a difference.

Summary:
The Msunduzi Municipality is fighting to keep landgrabbers off municipal owned land in Napierville – with a court interdict and regular demolition operations. But this hasn’t stopped a group of Municipal Officials, ex-cops and councilors have teamed up and are selling off municipal land around Pietermaritzburg.

Existing illegal developments cost the municipality millions of rands every year in lost revenue in terms of rates and service charges – but what to do regularize illegally built properties or demolish?

We look at the way forward for a Municipality that finds itself between a rock and a hard place.


Further information:
BACKGROUND
CURRENT SITUATION AT NAPIERVILLE:
For a mere R3000 you can get a plot and build your dream home. Double storeys welcome. Water and electricity to arranged – all ILLEGALLY of course!

The main suspects are Budget Dlamini – a Municipal Waste Dept employee – currently suspended and Mr. Dube – an ex-cop. Mr. Dlamini has already built his home and even farms a bit.

They have sold stands to at least 200 people – some have started building but have had their property demolished recently – there are some good guys in the Msundusi Municipality. There is a court order in favour of the Municipality who are the rightful owners – but that hasn’t stop the dynamic duo – of Dube and Dlamini.

RICHMOND ROAD DEVELOPMENT
This not the first time dodgy deals have gone down – there is an existing development on Richmond Road where people started building in 2017 – double storeys with water and electricity connections. The municipality missed the boat on this one and did not take action fast enough – with the newest sight, they are desperately trying to get on top of things. Some have suggested that the Municipality attempt to regularize the developments – but this would set a precedent and encourage further illegal activity,

LANDGRABBERS FIGHT BACK
The Dynamic Duo and their cronies are armed and often threaten police and municipal staff. They are still selling plots despite the demolishions last month.

We accompany the municipality on “clean up” operation, speak to local residents affected by illegal building, and hear from public economics experts about the impact of illegal landgrabbing on municipal finance.

The municipality is currently under administration and the administrator has actively been involved in trying to fight the Illegal Land Sales and will work with us on this one.

UNDERCOVER ELEMENT: – We make enquiries about buying a site for R3000.
CONFRONT

EXPOSING THE WEALTHY LANDGRABBERS
We go on a little door to door visit to some the more impressive mansions on Richmond Road – enquiring about title deeds, building plans and municipal rates and services accounts.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT
VO: Illegal Land invasions are not a new phenomenon. We have reported on land grabs from the Western Cape to Gauteng – exposing dodgy land sales and outright unlawful occupations.

LINK: The gap between land owners and the landless is widening, and while government fails to provide homes for the poor, syndicates are taking the gap with illegal land deals on land they do not own.

ROSS: this is a slap in the face to anyone that works hard and has put their life investment into a property and gone about it the right way, where people have gone under the radar and illegally built without any accountability.

VO: Msunduzi Municipality Ward Councillor, Ross Strachan, says Pietermaritzburg is being plagued by illegal land invasions. It’s not tribal land - but rather private and government owned land that’s being targeted - draining the municipal fiscus, and delaying future housing development projects.

Illegal Properties along the R56, just south of Pietermaritzburg, started popping up as far back as 2015 on private and government land. Today, some resemble those of posh suburbs in big cities. Double stories with top finishes and even some, with water features.

ROSS: This was a specific land grab that happened in this area. These are multi-million rand houses.
MAC: Do you think that there's a possibility that there could be, you know, building plans for any of these houses?
ROSS: Absolutely not. If there are building plans, they're not legal.

VO: The properties in question did not go through Town Planning processes.

KHOLISWA: You can see right from the outside, the owners are rich. They are well off people. Why are these people grabbing land unlawfully?

VO: This is an alarming trend, explains Kholiswa Malindini from the Wits School of Governance.

KHOLISWA: There is uneven enforcement of property rights. It could be people who have connections with those in authority.

MAC: Why did the municipality allow it to get to this stage?
ROSS: simply political interference. Nothing more. Nothing less.

VO: Msunduzi Municipality Mayor, Mzimkhulu Thebolla admits this is an irregular development that slipped through the cracks.

MAYOR: Unfortunately we were very late to respond by the time we started responding. Many houses had already been built. And as a result of that, some disciplinary action was taken against officials who were supposed to act at that period.

VO: But while these illegal properties along the R56 are still standing and occupied, it appears others in the Msunduzi are also taking a chance.

LINK: This is vacant land in Napierville. It's earmarked for Low-Cost residential housing. If you know the right people and act quick, you could snap up a plot for a fee, of course.

VO: We made a call to one of the alleged ringleaders in the community, Budget Dlamini.

BUDGET: The land isn’t for sale. No, you only pay the lawyer’s fees, the land you get for free
Agent: What do I pay? How much are the fees?
BUDGET: R3000

VO: Dlamini met the operative at the site the next day – showing him the lay of the land.

BUDGET: There’s free electricity (gas), everything for free. you see that one that has got cottage, even that one we took it by force.

VO: The land belongs to the Msunduzi Municipality. The land is not for free, and nor are the services - someone always pays. Philly (PHEELEE) Mhlongo is a legitimate home owner in Napierville – bordering the vacant land.

PHILLY: They are going to drag to the electricity and water from us. In all honesty, what’s happening here doesn’t sit well with us because in the end, it’ll bring down the value of our houses. We don’t want them to build here.

VO: But the opportunistic invaders are determined to take the land – and won’t hesitate to intimidate those, who stand in their way, explains Mhlongo.

PHILLY: The person who is selling the sites with his crew, they’ve got guns. And as the community we’ve got no guns. That’s a problem – how must we fight that? And they are intimidating us.

LINK: This is the modus operandi, you put up a quick makeshift structure, occupy it, and then it becomes much too complicated for the municipality to kick you out.

MAYOR: The people who are grabbing land in our city in the main are affluent people, Most of them are people who also understand the Bill of Rights.

VO: Mayor Thebolla believes educated people are trying to twist constitutional rights to their own advantage.

MAYOR: there's a high degree of misinterpretation of their human rights, because taking the land unlawfully is not allowed.
ROSS: looking at the vehicles that are driving in there, these aren't people that earn below the threshold. These are people that can well afford to buy property in a suburb and are working in kosher jobs.

VO: The same goes for the illegal properties on the R56 - those owners could and should be paying property taxes and services like refuse removal, sewage disposal, water and electricity.

MAC: Do these properties in any way contribute to municipal rates and services?
ROSS: No, they aren't. They aren’t recognized as part of our rate base. They have been recognized as taking our services illegally through illegal connections.

VO: Officially no municipal services are supplied to the area. While some houses get electricity from the Eskom supply, water is often illegally connected to the Umgeni Water Mainline.

Curious to find out what these homeowners have to say, I knocked on a few mansion doors.

MAC: rates and taxes, are you paying?
GOGO: I don’t want to talk too much about that. Because it is with the lawyers now

VO: The more we probed, the more reluctant she became to talk to us. (backs away slowly)

This lady recently bought the property from a previous owner.

MAC: Do you have a title deed?
LADY: I don't have a title deed for now
MAC: And rates and taxes are you paying?
LADY: We are not paying rates and taxes but we are willing to pay rates and taxes and we are willing to pay for services if the municipality can provide it the proper way.
MAC: So you’re staying here but water and electricity for free.
LADY: I won’t say Mahala, we are paying from our own pockets
MAC: And who are you paying?
LADY: We have our structures.

VO: Some said the owners were not home, //

MAC: Is your husband home?
LADY: NO, he ‘s not.

VO: Others ignored us completely and while some simply chased us away from the top floor of their mansion built illegally on land they do not own.

LADY ON PATIO: Don’t film the house!

LINK: So it looks like we've overstayed all welcome here. The community is becoming more and more hostile and nobody wants to speak to us yet this luxury cars that are driving in here. But are they paying the rates and taxes?

KHOLISWA: //we've seen quite a number of municipalities across the country are struggling when it comes to revenue generation. // it would have made a huge difference, a positive difference to them if they were to generate revenue from such structures.

VO: Back in Napierville, the structures that have started going up are not shacks either, notes Mayor Thebolla.

MAYOR: In the case of Napierville, you start to see wendy houses, truck loads of building material moving in.
MAC: Do you think they might be unaware that the land that they're buying is illegal or they're complicit in all of this?
MAYOR: The fact that they become so aggressive// whenever somebody tries to reason with them, it means they know that what they are doing is illegal.

ROSS: The current situation right now is absolute. I would say anarchy. They've basically forced their way in and started building on municipal land.

VO: The municipality believes some of these people are even government employees. We have established that Budget Dlamini, who met the undercover agent, is a Msunduzi Municipality employee, currently on suspension.

While we were filming the marked off plots, our presence was noted by, let’s call them, the developers, if you like.

LINK: A group just arrived here, threateningly came up to our camera crew and demanded that we stop filming - they wanted to take the cameras and delete footage. In the chaos of it all, we got to experience first-hand the intimidation tactics used by these people.

VO: They agreed to meet us the next day. This time round we had hidden cameras rolling from the start.

They insisted that we drive around the area first, showing us the houses that have already been built on the other side of the hill. We have subsequently established that area is predominantly tribal land, distributed by traditional leaders.

When we explained the issue was the municipal land aspect, the Napierville group was less open to engaging.

SPY GLASSES: GIRL : WE HERE AS THE RESIDENTS, WE HAVE NOTHING TO SAY….

VO: This young community representative, referred us to their legal advisor, but when we raised the issue of the undercover sting - Dlamini decided to speak.

MAC: What do you get for R3000?
BUDGET: You get nothing,
MAC: nothing

MAC: But you pay the to the lawyer to protect yourself, just in case the municipality comes and wants to take the land?
BUDGET: There is no proof that the land belongs to the municipality.

VO: We showed them the proof, a copy of the Msunduzi Municipality title deeds.

MAC: This is their land – this the title deed
BUDGET: It’s not true, it’s propaganda, I don’t think they are telling the truth.

VO: Mayor Thebolla is clear.

MAYOR: That is a municipal land as we speak.

VO: The Msunduzi Municipality even took the Napierville matter to court last year, and won the case.

MAYOR: We were able to get that court order, because that land, because it belongs to the municipality, we got a court order prohibiting anybody from settling on that land.

VO: But these land invaders feel entitled and show no respect for the rule of law.

KHOLISWA: From a governance perspective// this is also reflective of or indicative of weak political institutions in the area that is the municipality in this case.

VO: When we asked Dlamini about his current suspension from the Municipality - he was not phased at all.

MAC: Aren’t you worried that you’re going to get into trouble for being involved in this?
BUDGET I don’t care
MAC: Serious baba, You’re not scared of them
BUDGET: I’ve never been scared of them.

VO: The municipality has established a Rapid Response Unit. Mayor Thebolla explains that regular demolition operations are done at the Napierville site - three window to roof level formal structures have been destroyed, while demarcation tape and pegs are removed almost every week.

MAYOR: You deal with this today, next weekend here, people starting to move in, you remove them to day the next day, they are there.

VO: Resolving the illegal properties on parts of the R56 is a lot more tricky. While incorporating these houses into the rates base is an option, it could set a dangerous precedent, warns Strachan.

ROSS: The fact that people think they can build anyway. And then later on can be regularized. This needs to stop. This is a criminal activity and it needs to be treated as such.

VO: Mayor Thebolla is adamant that the Msunduzi Municipality will not allow any lawlessness.

MAYOR: We also don't want to promote any Banana Republic. We will apply the law that applies to everybody else in our country. What happened, on that R56. I can assure the people of Msunduzi and, the people of course of our province, that it will never happen again.

END


PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 21 seconds
VO: Next-level landgrabs in KwaZulu-Natal target government and private land. But hese brazen land invaders are not poor, they have means and have become a law unto themselves.

MAYOR: The people who are grabbing land in our city in the main are affluent people

VO: But what are authorities doing to curb this alarming trend?

PROMO 2 – 21 seconds
VO: A group of wealthy land invaders have teamed up to grab municipal and private land in Pietermaritzburg.

BUDGET: There’s free electricity (gas), everything for free.

VO: While landgrabbers are breaking ground in some areas, in others mansions have already been built illegally.

We investigate this alarming trend.


PROMO 3 – 11 seconds
VO: Free land, free municipal services - we investigate the audacious land grabs in KwaZulu Natal by people who have built mansions with water features and pools on stolen land.

BUDGET: There is no proof that the land belongs to the municipality. VO: We showed them the proof, a copy of the Msunduzi Municipality title deeds. MAC: This is their land – this the title deed BUDGET: It’s not true, it’s propaganda, I don’t think they are telling the truth. VO: Mayor Thebolla is clear. MAYOR: That is a municipal land as we speak. VO: The Msunduzi Municipality even took the Napierville matter to court last year, and won the case. MAYOR: We were able to get that court order, because that land, because it belongs to the municipality, we got a court order prohibiting anybody from settling on that land. VO: But these land invaders feel entitled and show no respect for the rule of law. KHOLISWA: From a governance perspective// this is also reflective of or indicative of weak political institutions in the area that is the municipality in this case. VO: When we asked Dlamini about his current suspension from the Municipality - he was not phased at all. MAC: Aren’t you worried that you’re going to get into trouble for being involved in this? BUDGET I don’t care MAC: Serious baba, You’re not scared of them BUDGET: I’ve never been scared of them. VO: The municipality has established a Rapid Response Unit. Mayor Thebolla explains that regular demolition operations are done at the Napierville site - three window to roof level formal structures have been destroyed, while demarcation tape and pegs are removed almost every week. MAYOR: You deal with this today, next weekend here, people starting to move in, you remove them to day the next day, they are there. VO: Resolving the illegal properties on parts of the R56 is a lot more tricky. While incorporating these houses into the rates base is an option, it could set a dangerous precedent, warns Strachan. ROSS: The fact that people think they can build anyway. And then later on can be regularized. This needs to stop. This is a criminal activity and it needs to be treated as such. VO: Mayor Thebolla is adamant that the Msunduzi Municipality will not allow any lawlessness. MAYOR: We also don't want to promote any Banana Republic. We will apply the law that applies to everybody else in our country. What happened, on that R56. I can assure the people of Msunduzi and, the people of course of our province, that it will never happen again. END PROMOS PROMO 1 – 21 seconds VO: Next-level landgrabs in KwaZulu-Natal target government and private land. But hese brazen land invaders are not poor, they have means and have become a law unto themselves. MAYOR: The people who are grabbing land in our city in the main are affluent people VO: But what are authorities doing to curb this alarming trend? PROMO 2 – 21 seconds VO: A group of wealthy land invaders have teamed up to grab municipal and private land in Pietermaritzburg. BUDGET: There’s free electricity (gas), everything for free. VO: While landgrabbers are breaking ground in some areas, in others mansions have already been built illegally. We investigate this alarming trend. PROMO 3 – 11 seconds VO: Free land, free municipal services - we investigate the audacious land grabs in KwaZulu Natal by people who have built mansions with water features and pools on stolen land.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Next Level Landgrabs in KZN – where mansions have illegally been built on government land by wealthy landgrabbers – we ask what the Msunduzi Municipality is doing to curb this alarming trend.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: SHOCK VALUE - the audacity of the people that have built mansions with fountains and pools on stolen land. WHY DO IT? Undercover, a confront and a municipality trying to make a difference.
metadata.Summary: The Msunduzi Municipality is fighting to keep landgrabbers off municipal owned land in Napierville – with a court interdict and regular demolition operations. But this hasn’t stopped a group of Municipal Officials, ex-cops and councilors have teamed up and are selling off municipal land around Pietermaritzburg. Existing illegal developments cost the municipality millions of rands every year in lost revenue in terms of rates and service charges – but what to do regularize illegally built properties or demolish? We look at the way forward for a Municipality that finds itself between a rock and a hard place.
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND CURRENT SITUATION AT NAPIERVILLE: For a mere R3000 you can get a plot and build your dream home. Double storeys welcome. Water and electricity to arranged – all ILLEGALLY of course! The main suspects are Budget Dlamini – a Municipal Waste Dept employee – currently suspended and Mr. Dube – an ex-cop. Mr. Dlamini has already built his home and even farms a bit. They have sold stands to at least 200 people – some have started building but have had their property demolished recently – there are some good guys in the Msundusi Municipality. There is a court order in favour of the Municipality who are the rightful owners – but that hasn’t stop the dynamic duo – of Dube and Dlamini. RICHMOND ROAD DEVELOPMENT This not the first time dodgy deals have gone down – there is an existing development on Richmond Road where people started building in 2017 – double storeys with water and electricity connections. The municipality missed the boat on this one and did not take action fast enough – with the newest sight, they are desperately trying to get on top of things. Some have suggested that the Municipality attempt to regularize the developments – but this would set a precedent and encourage further illegal activity, LANDGRABBERS FIGHT BACK The Dynamic Duo and their cronies are armed and often threaten police and municipal staff. They are still selling plots despite the demolishions last month. We accompany the municipality on “clean up” operation, speak to local residents affected by illegal building, and hear from public economics experts about the impact of illegal landgrabbing on municipal finance. The municipality is currently under administration and the administrator has actively been involved in trying to fight the Illegal Land Sales and will work with us on this one. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT: – We make enquiries about buying a site for R3000. CONFRONT EXPOSING THE WEALTHY LANDGRABBERS We go on a little door to door visit to some the more impressive mansions on Richmond Road – enquiring about title deeds, building plans and municipal rates and services accounts.
